ordered_diagnoses: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy with Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction

s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of abdominal pain and syncope following alcohol ingestion with a prolonged time course
salient_findings: Recurrent abdominal pain after alcohol ingestion
High-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions on ECG
ST segment elevations and depressions on ECG
key_facts: Patient presented with recurrent abdominal pain
Symptoms occurred 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion
Symptoms lasted 5-10 minutes
Syncope occurred only after large alcohol intake
Patient has a history of hypertension
Patient has a history of smoking and alcohol overconsumption
High-sensitivity troponin I was normal
Serum potassium was normal
ECG showed high-degree atrioventricular block and premature ventricular contractions
ECG showed ST segment elevations and depressions
Coronary angiography showed 10% stenosis in proximal LAD and RCA

shortlist.label: Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of long-term alcohol overconsumption and symptoms consistent with cardiomyopathy

shortlist.label: Vasospastic Angina
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings of ST segment elevations and coronary angiography showing minimal stenosis, consistent with vasospastic angina

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy with Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: History of hypertension and symptoms consistent with obstructive cardiomyopathy

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: ECG findings of premature ventricular contractions and ventricular tachycardia, consistent with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Symptoms of recurrent abdominal pain and syncope, potentially related to catecholamine surges

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including recurrent abdominal pain and syncope, occurred 6-20 hours after alcohol ingestion, which is consistent with vasospastic angina triggered by alcohol consumption. The ECG findings of ST segment elevations and depressions also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Alcoholic Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of alcohol overconsumption, the coronary angiography showed only mild stenosis, and the symptoms are more consistent with vasospastic angina.

rejected.label: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy with Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction
rejected.why: There is no mention of left ventricular outflow tract obstruction or hypertrophy on the coronary angiography or ECG findings.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The ECG findings do not show typical signs of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, such as T-wave inversion or epsilon waves.

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are not typical of pheochromocytoma, and there is no mention of other characteristic signs such as hypertension paroxysms or elevated catecholamines.
